 Verifying your income and reviewing your deductions 'could save you potential penalties down the track'. The deadline to get your tax in falls on Monday, November 2 this year. · Getty Nick Whigham · Head of Yahoo Finance Australia Thu 29 October 2026 at 5:28 pm GMT-4 4 min read About a million Aussies are being urged to lodge their personal tax return with just a few days left before the deadline . The ATO's traditional deadline falls on a Saturday this year, so workers have some extra time with the deadline pushed back to midnight on Monday, November 2. 
 If taxpayers haven't self-lodged their tax return by that time, or engaged with a professional to lodge on their behalf, the tax office can apply penalties. That can start at $364 and increase the later its filed. 
 "The ATO has received over 10 million income tax returns with around 1 million self-preparers still yet to lodge," a spokesperson told Yahoo Finance . 
 The tax office is also reminding retirees and lower-income earners who might mistakenly think they don't need to file a return. 
 "Even if you have legitimately left the tax system, income from events such as selling an investment property can create lodgement obligations," it says. "If tax was withheld from your income from an employer, even if you earn below the tax-free threshold, you still need to lodge and it could result in a refund of that tax." 
 RELATED 
 Uptick in Aussies switching their super to cash amid market volatility 
 Bunnings, Kmart boss take huge swipe at tax settings 
 ATO admits wrong assumption played into cutting off credit cards 
 The ATO now has more than 100 million pieces of information it has pre-filled into individual tax returns . That includes information from employers, banks, health insurers, share registries, service providers and government agencies. 
 That makes lodging your tax return easier than ever, with ATO Assistant Commissioner Anita Challen saying "it takes on average 8 minutes to lodge a return using myTax". 
 But Aussies are still urged to make sure the pre-filled data is correct – because that's not always the case. 
 "Pre-fill is useful, but people shouldn't treat it as a substitute for checking their own records," H&R Block's Director of Tax Communications, Mark Chapman, told Yahoo Finance . 
 And lodging your return with incorrect pre-filled data can lead to a "follow up". 
 "Our research found nearly half of Australians had experienced a surprising tax outcome at some point, whether that was a lower refund, an unexpected bill or contact from the ATO," he said. 
 What to keep in mind when lodging your tax return 
 With just a few days left to beat the deadline, industry experts say it's still better to get things right rather than rush just to file on time. 
 Susan Franks, Tax Leader at Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, said it's not worth risking avoidable mistake just to get your return in before the Monday deadline. 
 Story continues "Tax time isn't just about meeting a deadline. It's about making sure your return is accurate, complete and supported by the right information," she said. 
 "With the 2 November deadline only days away, taking an hour today to double-check your records, verify your income and review your deductions could save you time, stress and potential penalties down the track." 
 MORE: Landlords, WFH, side hustles and crypto – what the ATO is targeting this year 
 If you're on the books of a registered accountant by the close of business today, you'll generally have until 15 May 2027 to lodge your return, she added. 
 The peak accounting body has issued a list of five key things for people to remember if they're doing their return this weekend. 
 The $1,000 instant tax deduction doesn't start until next financial year. You may have heard about the new change which means Aussies can automatically claim $1,000 in work deductions without receipts or any questions asked. But that doesn't start until next year's tax return. 
 Review your working from home expenses and make sure you're using the correct method and have records. "Working-from-home deductions remain a source of confusion for many taxpayers and mistakes can lead to claims being reduced or rejected," Franks said. 
 Side hustle income need to be included. Extra income from online content creation, short-term rentals, delivery or ride-sharing apps and other digital platforms must be declared. 
 Don't forget about shares and crypto . Properly consider any gains or losses before lodging their return. 
 Remember to claim eligible donations . Make sure any donations made to registered Deductible Gift Recipients are properly recorded and included so you don't miss out on deductions.
